sentiment.instructions: Judge the overall sentiment of the tweet: the author's own feeling, or, for news-style headlines, the clear valence of the reported event. Pick neutral only when the tweet is mainly informational or has no discernible feeling either way.

criteria.positive:
Any enjoyment, enthusiasm, praise, love, gratitude, hope, prayer, well-wishing, encouragement or anticipation, even mild ('perfect night', 'I will celebrate', 'can't wait', 'for sure going to', 'hope', ':-)'). Also includes:
- Upbeat invitations and promotions offering something fun, free or exciting: 'come join', 'come support', 'get your tickets', giveaways, prizes, 'free'.
- Headlines reporting clearly good events: wins, titles, achievements, celebrations, people delighted.
criteria.neutral:
Includes:
- Purely factual news or routine reports with no clearly good or bad event.
- Dry logistical notices: date, place, 'RSVP', 'register'.
- Questions, polls, rumors, trivia, and requests or pleas to celebrities.
- Plans stated flatly, and detached play-by-play or wry commentary on public figures, teams or companies that shows no clear hostility.
criteria.negative:
Includes:
- The author's own disappointment, sadness, dread, boredom, frustration, missing out, or self-deprecation, even when joking ('going to die', 'no talent', 'can't go', 'bummer', ':(').
- Clear criticism, mockery, sarcasm, hostility, or pointed rhetorical questions aimed at people, groups or politicians.
- Headlines reporting clearly bad events: attacks, deaths, arrests, injuries, deficits, scandals, defects.
